name: PREVPROL
aliases: PFMT for secondary prevention of prolapse
question: Does supervised pelvic floor muscle training reduce later prolapse symptoms in women with untreated stage I–III prolapse compared with lifestyle advice alone?

design.blinding: Participants and physiotherapists unmasked; data entry staff and statistician masked

arms.label: Supervised pelvic floor muscle training, Pilates-based classes and lifestyle leaflet

design.population: 414 women from a 1993–1994 birth cohort, recruited 14–17 years after index delivery at three UK and New Zealand centers, with stage I–III prolapse and no previous prolapse treatment (stages 0 and IV excluded; 399/412 analyzed, 96.8%, had prolapse above or at the hymen).

verdictNote: The two-year symptom advantage was small; a later UK-only conference report found no difference at three years.
takeaway: In women with untreated stage I–III prolapse, supervised pelvic floor muscle training plus Pilates-based classes and a lifestyle leaflet lowered two-year POP-SS versus a lifestyle leaflet alone (adjusted mean difference −1.01 points, 95% CI −1.70 to −0.33).

reports.label: Three-year UK follow-up (conference abstract)
reports.dateLocator: ICS 2016 scientific program, Friday September 16, abstract 430
reports.citation: Hagen S, Glazener C, McClurg D, et al. "A Multicentre Randomised Controlled Trial of a Pelvic Floor Muscle Training Intervention for the Prevention of Pelvic Organ Prolapse: 3 Year Follow-up." *International Continence Society Annual Meeting.* 2016;Abstract 430.
reports.noDoi: ICS conference abstract 430 has no DOI or PMID located
reports.followUp: Three years; UK subgroup, 335 analyzed after two postrandomization exclusions

results.measure: Mean POP-SS at three years; adjusted mean difference, PFMT minus leaflet
results.note: Three-year analysis restricted to UK participants; outcome was the original trial's primary measure at a later time point, with 70% questionnaire response.

results.measure: Any prolapse-related treatment within three years, UK respondents
results.note: Includes clinical consultations and referrals, not only surgery or pessary use.

reports.label: Primary two-year report
reports.citation: Hagen S, Glazener C, McClurg D, et al. "Pelvic Floor Muscle Training for Secondary Prevention of Pelvic Organ Prolapse (PREVPROL): A Multicentre Randomised Controlled Trial." *Lancet.* 2017;389(10067):393-402. doi:10.1016/S0140-6736(16)32109-2
reports.followUp: Two years after randomization; 412 analyzed after two postrandomization exclusions
reports.followUpLocator: Accepted manuscript PDF pp8–9, Figure 1, Table 2

results.measure: Mean seven-item POP-SS at two years (0–28, symptoms during preceding four weeks, lower better); adjusted mean difference, PFMT minus leaflet
results.note: Repeated-measures model adjusted for age, minimization variables and baseline POP-SS; prespecified two-sided alpha 0.05. Difference was below the 1.52-point minimally important change derived from a surgical prolapse cohort.
results.locator: Accepted manuscript PDF p9, Table 2; p7 statistical analysis

results.measure: Any prolapse-related treatment within two years, among women answering both annual questions
results.note: Includes clinical consultations and referrals; surgery and pessary use were uncommon.

results.measure: ICIQ-UI SF at two years; adjusted mean difference, PFMT minus leaflet
results.note: Any urine leakage and weekly pad use did not differ significantly.

harms.label: Reported adverse events
harms.note: One fall before a Pilates class, one episode of tailbone pain during training, and one episode of chest pain with shortness of breath during training.

delivery.label: Training program
delivery.value: Five specialist physiotherapy visits over 16 weeks with individualized home exercises three times daily, two offered six-week Pilates-based class blocks, home DVD, and annual physiotherapy reviews; both groups received the lifestyle leaflet.

delivery.label: Physiotherapy attendance
delivery.value: In the intervention arm, 19 women attended no individual visits and 88 attended all five; mean 3.5 visits (SD 1.7).

delivery.label: Training at two years
delivery.note: Self-reported pelvic floor exercises during the preceding four weeks; denominators not specified in the prose.

delivery.label: Surgery and pessary use within two years
delivery.note: Respondents reporting treatment at both follow-up questionnaires; these are sparse secondary outcomes.

relations.note: POPPY established a symptom benefit from supervised training in treatment-seeking women; PREVPROL tested prevention in untreated prolapse.
